title: Exact Sine of pi over Six
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Without a calculator, use the unit circle or a special triangle to find the exact value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.

steps.title: Translate the Radian Measure
steps.explanation: The angle sits in the first quadrant at $30^{\circ}$ above the positive $x$-axis.
steps.why: Converting radians to familiar degree measures helps locate the reference triangle.

steps.title: Use the 30-60-90 Triangle
steps.explanation: In a $30^{\circ}$-$60^{\circ}$-$90^{\circ}$ triangle the side opposite $30^{\circ}$ is half the hypotenuse.
steps.why: Special right triangles give exact ratios without decimal approximation.

steps.title: Confirm the Sign on the Unit Circle
steps.explanation: The unit-circle point at angle $\pi/6$ has $y$-coordinate $1/2$, and first-quadrant sine is positive.
steps.why: Sine equals the $y$-coordinate of the unit-circle point.
